volume.method: mean daily pool volume, last 30 complete days

volatility.method: sample stdev of 88 daily log returns × √365

curve.method: active L rebuilt from 590 initialized ticks (liquidityNet) around the current tick

breakEven.basis: static fees, expected result vs holding

scenarios.description: ETH moves steadily (log-linear) to each price over the horizon; fees accrue while inside the range at the in-range rate

comparison.basis: same simulated paths for every row; history column re-centres each range on every past day

assumptions.text: Fee share at price P = your L ÷ (pool L(P) + your L). 'follow' keeps pool L at today's active L wherever price goes (LPs re-centre); 'static' reads pool L(P) from today's on-chain liquidity map.
Pool volume per day stays at the selected level (default: 30-day mean). Real volume rises with volatility and is bursty.
Forward prices follow driftless geometric Brownian motion at realized volatility. Real ETH returns have fat tails, so extremes are understated.
Fees accrue at 0.05% of volume while in range; no compounding; protocol fee off.
Historical figures use GeckoTerminal daily candles; time in range per day assumes prices are spread evenly between low and high.
Gas is a flat USD cost for mint, collect and burn. No rebalancing.
Competition is the liquidity visible at the snapshot block. Just-in-time liquidity (added and removed around single swaps) is not visible, so fee share is overstated, most of all in thin pools.
